q-161593.name: Question 1
q-161593.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252181/assets/80bde6a20ceed7c052a87eda6f05c542f6046de7014f6402f5f453b6610f8d42.png)

Consider the set $A,$ shown above. The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-161593.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252181/assets/05b25521109f373e2a7718523ce6289b27b37bd185d4fc60f0d052c232f4f8a4.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the line $y=-1+x.$

Therefore, 

$$
∂A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y=-1+x\,\}.
$$

?

Consider the set A, shown above. The boundary of A is given by ∂A={(x,y)∈R2:AAAAA}. What is the missing expression?

a
x2+4y2>36
b
x2+4y2<36
c
x2+4y2=36
d
x2+4y2≤36
e
x2+4y2≥36
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The boundary of a set A, denoted ∂A, is the set that contains all the boundary points of A.

The set A and its boundary ∂A are shown below.

q-161718.name: Question 5
q-161718.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252181/assets/af1e6e7b384732a527fc77e9729c6e02aaa288d4076c030c9fae58742cb10f74.png)

Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is 

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<2,\,\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAA}}\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-161718.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252181/assets/0a0b92621d83d6395926a75b5cae34f479a8b9e64dfe82711094c3724b3b3220.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252181/assets/3ddef68bf4b4284c1b68896920fddb8d7fb0e70eba15dee103cdbc0134a9ed20.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<2,\,-x<y<x\}.
$$
